steps.player: How are you doing?

steps.npc: I'm happy.

steps.player: Really?

steps.npc: Really.

steps.player: Really, really?

steps.npc: Really, really.

steps.player: Really, really rea...

steps.npc: Stop right there.

steps.player: Where?

steps.npc: There.

steps.player: Here?

steps.npc: No, there.

steps.player: Argh! Now you're at it.

steps.npc: At what?

steps.player: It.

steps.npc: What's it?

steps.player: You know... it...

steps.npc: Stop, stop, stop! Right, we're going to play a little game now.

steps.player: Is it going to be fun? Is it? Is it? Is it?

steps.npc: It's called give the cat some peace.

steps.player: How do you play?

steps.npc: You gently stroke your cat, then pick it up, and finally, you leave it for an extended snooze in your backpack.

steps.player: That doesn't sound like much fun. I'd rather spend quality time annoying you.

steps.npc: I'd never have guessed. Well in that case, I would be really annoyed if you took me hunting rats.

steps.player: Really?

steps.npc: Really.
HISS!

steps.player: How old are you now?

steps.npc: I'm happy.

steps.player: I thought I asked you your age, not how you were?

steps.npc: Oh! My fault. To answer your question, I'd like to go to the Varrock Sewers.

steps.player: What? Are you listening to me?

steps.npc: It's a quarter past Caistleday.

steps.player: Are you trying to dodge the question?

steps.npc: I think your amulet might be on the blink. Meoow, Miiiaaoow!

steps.text: You examine the Amulet of Catspeak carefully.

steps.player: Strange, it looks okay to me.

steps.npc: Hiss's'sss's. ~Your cat tries to hold in a snicker, but fails miserably.

options.text: Where do you want to go?

steps.player: Where do you want to go?

steps.npc: Well one place I don't want to go is the rat pits.

steps.player: Why's that?

steps.npc: All the other cats will make fun of me, I'm so badly out of shape. Take me hunting.

steps.player: Don't worry cat, I'll get you back in shape.

options.text: What do you want to do now?

steps.player: What do you want to do now?

steps.npc: I'm happy just pottering around.

steps.player: Do you fancy a bit of hunting?

steps.npc: To be perfectly honest, I'd rather just lay about and groom myself. Looking at the state of your gear, you would do well to follow suit.

steps.player: There's nothing wrong with how I'm dressed.

steps.npc: That dragon armour you're wearing is so, like, last year.
That thing you're wearing is so, like, last year.

steps.player: I refuse to take fashion advice from a cat - a fat lazy one to boot!

steps.npc: Meeoow! Someone's feeling touchy!

steps.player: That's the last time I ask you what you want to do.
How are you doing?

steps.npc: I'm content. A little more action might be good, but then again you might ruffle up my fur and then I'd have to groom all over again.

steps.player: Pah! You're the laziest old bag of fluff I've ever met.
How old are you now?

steps.npc: A little older than I was before, but not as old as I will be in a moment.

steps.player: What kind of answer is that?

steps.npc: Well, your idea of time and mine are too different for either of us to understand the other.

steps.player: Um... I don't really get it.

steps.npc: Well for one, I don't count the time I spend in your Bank - which is horribly boring - nor in your bag.

steps.player: Well that's not too complicated.

steps.npc: I'm just getting started. Now there is also a difference in cat years and human years. To approximate time in cat years you take a value in years, subtract 1, multiply it by 4, and then add 16.

steps.player: So... if a cat is newly born it's already 12 cat years old?

steps.npc: I said approximate not calculate. Anyway it only works once the cat is 1 year old.
The last complication is that time doesn't actually seem to move, outside of cats ageing.

steps.player: Anyway, back to the question. How old are you in cat years?

steps.npc: I don't know. I'm a cat, I can't do maths!

steps.player: Hmph!

options.text: Where do you want to go?

steps.player: Where do you want to go?

steps.npc: Somewhere nice and quiet. I'm a bit behind in my snoozing schedule.

options.text: What do you want to do now?

steps.player: What do you want to do now?

steps.npc: Sleep.

steps.player: How am I going to get you back in shape if all you want to do is sleep?

steps.npc: Surgery. That's the answer to all our problems.

steps.player: Well smarty pants, where am I going to find a cosmetic surgeon who's willing to perform liposuction on a cat around here?

steps.npc: I don't know. To be honest I don't even know what those things are.

steps.player: Me neither, actually...
How are you doing?

steps.npc: Hiss! What do you care?

steps.player: Oh come on, you're not going to have a hissy fit with me now are you?

steps.npc: Hiss!

steps.player: Oh dear.
How old are you now?

steps.npc: I'd rather not say.

steps.player: Oh come on, tell me.

steps.npc: Okay, I'm very old and fat! Are you happy now? Do you feel good, having a laugh at my expense?

steps.player: Oh cat, I'm sorry. I didn't mean it like that. How can I make it up to you?

steps.npc: Well, maybe if you stroked me the odd time, or played with me...

options.text: Where do you want to go?

steps.player: Where do you want to go?

steps.npc: Back to the pits. I want to tell the ratcatchers what a rotten master you've been.

steps.player: What? You wouldn't do that would you?

steps.npc: If you paid me a little more attention I wouldn't, but I must admit I have been tempted for some time.

steps.player: Look cat, I promise I'll try to be a better friend to you from now on.

steps.npc: I'll believe it when I see it.

options.text: What do you want to do now?

steps.player: What do you want to do now?

steps.npc: I'd like to go hunting, but since you've been neglecting me I'm too fat to do that properly anymore.

steps.player: Oh come on! I'm sure you're not that bad at hunting.

steps.npc: You're having a laugh! I couldn't even catch a cold.

steps.player: Hmm.. I think we may have to work on your self esteem. With an attitude like yours it's no wonder you can't catch rats.

steps.npc: Hiss! The reason I can't catch any is because you neglect me.
leaving me in the Bank or in your bags for extended periods is not conducive to proper exercise!

steps.player: Um... sorry?

steps.npc: Hmph!

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.npc: Sorry human, but what are you wearing?

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.player: I got some cat ears made for me, don't they look meeeeeeeooooowvalous.

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.text: The cat looks you dead in the eye, unblinking.

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.npc: Am I a joke to you?

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.player: I thought it'd be cute and funny.

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-with-a-c.npc: It's not, take them off now human, before I get myself a pair of human ears to wear.

steps.npc: Purr...purr...

steps.prompt: Are you sure you want to shoo away the cat?

steps.player: That's it, scram, go away and don't come back, you big sack of laziness.

steps.npc: Hiss! I can't believe I wasted so much of my time with you. Pah! Next time I'll find a proper adventurer as a companion.

steps.player: Shoo cat!

steps.npc: Meeeooow!

steps.text: You choose not to shoo away the cat.

chasing-crypt-rats.player: Are you up for some rodent catching?
Come on lazy boots, crack on!

chasing-crypt-rats.npc: No way! It's not that I'm lazy, no no I'll rephrase that, laziness aside I'm still not going to do that.
I'm not some crazy kamikazee cat, I want get old and live a quiet peacful life, close to a nice warm fire.

chasing-crypt-rats.player: Pah you're just a big scardy cat.

training-into-a-wily-cat.text: Your cat, through exercise has shrunk, into a wily cat.

placing-into-the-pet-basket.text: The cat goes to sleep on the blanket.
